Concept Description: Whether the participant has had percutaneous coronary angioplasty (balloon dilation of a coronary artery, usually with stent placement; also called PTCA or PCI), from self-report, a hospital record or a death record. Use when the source asks about coronary angioplasty, PTCA, PCI or coronary stent placement; not for diagnostic coronary angiography or cardiac catheterization alone, for carotid or peripheral-artery angioplasty, or for bypass surgery (see History of coronary artery bypass graft).

Concept Description: Whether the participant has had coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery, from self-report, a hospital record or a death record. Use when the source asks about coronary bypass or CABG; not for coronary angioplasty or stenting (see History of coronary angioplasty), other revascularization, or valve surgery.

Concept Description: Whether the participant has an implanted cardiac pacemaker (device present, or an implant recorded), from a questionnaire, screening form, ECG or hospital abstraction. Use when the source states a pacemaker is present or was implanted, including a biventricular (CRT) pacemaker; not for a defibrillator or other implanted device on its own, or for a pacemaker check or interrogation visit. Composite items are lossy: the MRI screening example 'Do you have a cardiac pacemaker or a heart valve prosthesis?' is yes for a prosthetic valve alone, so map it to PRESENT only with a proposal flag (it overstates pacemaker prevalence).
